points.title: Why 1 hex digit = 4 bits
points.must: 4 bits have 2⁴ = 16 patterns and hex has 16 digits, so each nibble is one hex digit; a byte = exactly 2 hex digits; denary has no such link.
points.model: 4 bits → 2⁴ = 16 patterns; hex has 16 digits (0–F) → one hex digit = exactly one nibble. One byte = 2 hex digits (00–FF). 10 is not a power of 2, so denary digits do not match groups of bits.

points.title: Nibble table
points.must: The 16 nibbles 0000–1111 with hex and denary; work out with 8 4 2 1.

points.title: Binary → hex
points.must: Steps: groups of 4 from the right, pad left, each group → digit; example 1111101001 = 3E9.
points.model: Group in 4s from the right, pad the left group with zeros, replace each group. 1111101001 → 0011 1110 1001 → 3E9₁₆. 1011 0111 → B7; 101 1011 → 0101 1011 → 5B; keep middle zeros: 0001 0000 0110 → 106.

points.title: Hex → binary
points.must: Each digit → exactly 4 bits including leading zeros inside; example 2F = 0010 1111, A0 = 1010 0000.
points.model: Replace each hex digit with 4 bits. 2F → 0010 1111. A0 → 1010 0000 (the 0000 must stay). 1A3 → 0001 1010 0011.

points.title: Octal vs hex grouping
points.must: 3 bits vs 4 bits; byte = 2 hex digits but not a whole number of octal digits; octal ↔ hex via binary (755₈ = 1ED₁₆).
points.model: Octal: 3 bits per digit; hex: 4 bits per digit. Bytes/words are multiples of 4 → whole hex digits. 755₈ → 111 101 101 → 0001 1110 1101 → 1ED₁₆ (= 493).

points.title: Hex is a representation for humans
points.must: Computer stores and processes only binary; hex changes how values are shown, not stored.
points.model: Hexadecimal is a way of displaying binary to people. Inside the computer everything is binary. Hex does NOT save memory and does NOT make processing faster.

points.title: Advantage: shorter
points.must: 4 times shorter than binary; byte = 2 digits not 8; 32-bit address = 8 digits; shorter than denary for big values.
points.model: Each hex digit replaces 4 bits → 4× shorter. 1 byte: 2 hex digits vs 8 bits. 32-bit address: 8 hex digits. FFFFFFFF vs 4 294 967 295.

points.title: Advantage: easier to read, fewer errors
points.must: Chain: shorter → easier to read/remember/copy → fewer human errors; example 0111111111101001 vs 7FE9.
points.model: Shorter → easier for people to read, remember and copy → fewer mistakes (skipping/swapping bits). 0111111111101001₂ = 7FE9₁₆.

points.title: Advantage: easy conversion and fits bytes
points.must: Direct 4-bit mapping (no division as with denary), shows which bits are set (0x80, 0x0F); bytes and words are whole numbers of hex digits.
points.model: Conversion hex ↔ binary is a look-up of 16 patterns, unlike denary which needs division. You can see the bits: 0x80 = only top bit set, 0x0F = low 4 bits set. Bytes/16/32/64-bit words = 2/4/8/16 hex digits.

points.title: Colour codes
points.must: #RRGGBB: 3 bytes = 24 bits; example #1F4FD8 = R 31, G 79, B 216; #000000 black, #FFFFFF white.
points.model: Colour = #RRGGBB, each pair one byte 00–FF (0–255), total 24 bits = 6 hex digits. #1F4FD8: red 1F = 31, green 4F = 79, blue D8 = 216. #FF0000 red, #000000 black, #FFFFFF white.

points.title: Memory addresses, dumps, machine code, error codes
points.must: Definitions of memory address and memory dump; examples 0x7FFE4A10, B8 04 00 CD 21, 0x80070005.
points.model: Memory address = unique binary number identifying a memory location, shown in hex (0x7FFE4A10). Memory dump = memory contents shown as hex byte pairs (B8 04 00 CD 21) for debugging. Error codes such as 0x80070005 are compact to report.

points.title: MAC and IPv6 addresses
points.must: MAC = 48 bits = 12 hex digits in 6 pairs (3C:52:82:1A:9F:04); IPv6 = 128 bits = 32 hex digits in 8 groups.
points.model: MAC address = 48-bit physical address of a network card, 12 hex digits: 3C:52:82:1A:9F:04. IPv6 = 128 bits written as 8 groups of 4 hex digits: 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:ff00:0042:8329.

points.title: Character codes
points.must: Unicode code points in hex: A = U+0041, Ә = U+04D8; HTML Ә.
points.model: Character code points are listed in hex: A = U+0041 (65), Kazakh Ә = U+04D8. In HTML: Ә.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: At least three: hex saves memory/faster (wrong); grouping from the left; MAC = 12 bits; advantage without explanation.
points.model: Wrong: 'hex uses less memory / is faster'. Group bits from the RIGHT. MAC = 12 hex digits = 48 bits. For 'explain' give the advantage AND why (shorter → fewer errors).
